learning: If line_loss_events fall to 0 while max_error stays near 0.06 m, the limit is lag, so move the sensor bar forward to y = 0.06 m next. If line losses remain at 1, coverage is not the cause, and the footprint is not the lever.
notes: Robot package for the 16 mm footprint test. Only sensor_size changes from the iteration 2 design, so the result is attributable to footprint. Controller is held fixed at iteration 2 values.
rationale: Iteration 2 (entityR2B, score 53.3054) and iterations 0 and 1 all ended off_track in all 60 trials per design. Max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.066 m, the off-track floor, and line_loss_events is 1 to 2 per run. Steering_oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.16), so the robot drifts steadily rather than jittering. Sensor pitch at 10, 15 and 20 mm did not change max_error or line losses, and the 0.10 m track and kp 1.4 did not move max_error either. Coverage at the outer sensors is the one untested variable the Builder has identified, so this iteration changes only sensor_size, from 0.012 to 0.016 m, and keeps every other value from the iteration 2 design. I kept the controller identical to iteration 2 (kp 1.4, kd 0.15, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). Changing gains as well would confound the footprint test. The 16 mm footprint covers more of the outer sensors' area at a given offset, so line losses should fall if coverage is the cause. Expected: line_loss_events toward 0. Max_error may stay near 0.06 m, which would point to lag as the remaining limit.
